headline: Found buildings in the 56 Margin Street project not preferably preserved, and granted 44 Derby Street 18 months to move line sets indoors.
summary: Harborlight Homes and Lifebridge asked to demolish two buildings and partly demolish one on Margin Street, with 41 new supportive housing apartments planned. Four applications were continued to November 18, and requests at 1A Cambridge Street and 11 Summer Street were withdrawn. A cedar fence at 169 Federal Street was approved with design conditions.
decisions: Accepted the withdrawal of the solar application at 1A Cambridge Street without prejudice, with 5 members in favor.
Approved the cedar fence at 169 Federal Street as submitted, with conditions on the posts and gate, by roll call of all six members present.
Granted the applicant 18 months to move the heat pump line sets indoors, with Mr. Murray recused; if not finished, the applicant must return to the commission.
Continued the 107 Federal Street application to November 18.
Continued the 396 Essex Street door application to November 18 for a site visit.
Found 20 Endicott, 54 Margin, 56 Margin, and 24 Endicott historically significant, with all six members present in favor.
Found the buildings not preferably preserved, excepting the stated facade conditions, with Ms. English voting no.
Continued the 21 Warren Street chimney removal application to November 18.
Accepted the withdrawal of the demolition delay request for the carriage building at 11 Summer Street.
Continued the 7 Carpenter Street heat pump application to November 18, in the applicant's absence.
Gave a CLG opinion supporting the National Register eligibility of the Church of the Immaculate Conception Complex, with all six members present in favor.
Approved the October 7 meeting minutes, with all six members present in favor.

plain_text:
DRAFT 
SALEM HISTORICAL COMMISSION 
MINUTES 
November 4, 2026 
 
A meeting of the Salem Historical Commission was held on November 4, 2026 at 6:00PM via Zoom 
Virtual Meeting.  Present were Mark Meche, Milo Martinez, Robert Peterson, Brendan Murray, Chair 
Kelly Tyler-Lewis, Vice Chair Rebecca English. Staff: Patti Kelleher. Absent: Margarida Raka-
Goncalves, Emily Gonzalez, Vijay Joyce. 
 
 
348 Essex Street 
Andrea Bennett applied for a Certificate of Appropriateness to replace 3tab asphalt shingles with 
architectural shingles.   
 
This application was reviewed as a minor change under the Historical Commission policy for architectural 
roof shingles. No objection was received, and a Certificate was issued on October 27, 2026.  
 
 
59 Summer Street 
Daniel and Michelle Finamore applied for a Certificate of Appropriateness to replace 3tab asphalt 
shingles with architectural shingles.   
 
This application was reviewed as a minor change under the Historical Commission policy for architectural 
roof shingles. No objection was received, and a Certificate was issued on November 2, 2026.  
 
 
1A Cambridge Street–continuation 
Eleanor Uddo applied for a Certificate of Appropriateness to install solar.   
 
The applicant requested to withdraw without prejudice.  
 
VOTE:  Mr. Martinez motioned to accept the applicant’s request to withdraw the existing application 
without prejudice.  Mr. Peterson seconded the motion.  Roll Call: Meche, Martinez, Peterson, Murray, 
Tyler-Lewis were in favor and the motion so carried. 
 
 
169 Federal Street–continuation 
Alicia and Brian Peters applied for a Certificate of Appropriateness for fencing.   
 
Mr. Peters noted a chain link fence in the rear of the yard was visible from Kelleher Way and another 
fence would be visible from Federal Street.  A site visit had occurred and was attended by Mr. Peterson, 
who said that the fencing in the backyard would be replicated on other sides of the property.  Mr. Peterson 
said the fence would be cedar and that the posts on the fence should have simple caps, flat cap rail on rear 
fence line; front-mounted panels to conceal posts on the driveway.  Mr. Peterson said that the height 
should match existing.  Mr. Meche showed a plan of the proposed fence as well as submitted images.  Mr. 
Peters said every component of the fence would be cedar.
Salem Historical Commission Meeting Minutes, November 4, 2026 
Page 2 of 7 
 
Mr. Meche clarified where and how much fencing would be installed.  Mr. Peters cited the fence at 93 
Federal Street as inspiration for the design to emulate.  Ms. Kelleher said that the requested fence also 
featured on Cambridge Street.  Mr. Martinez clarified that the rear yard board fence had limited visibility.  
Ms. Kelleher added that that fence was in accordance with the SHC design guidelines.  Chair Tyler-Lewis 
expressed preference for hidden posts at the front of a property and tolerance for exposed posts in the rear.  
Mr. Meche wanted to see the posts cut off (at an angle) from the top of the fence in the rear.  Mr. Peters 
noted the vendor having discouraged painting cedar. 
 
No public comment. 
 
Mr. Peters requested recommendations for fence builders. 
 
VOTE:  Mr. Martinez motioned to approve the application as submitted with option to replace pyramid 
caps in rear with scarf cut on the posts; the front fence to be built such that panels were in front of 
hidden/concealed posts, with gate (retaining its swoop) appearing to have a continuous run.  Mr. Meche 
seconded the motion.  Roll Call: English, Meche, Martinez, Peterson, Murray, Tyler-Lewis were in favor 
and the motion so carried. 
 
 
44 Derby Street–continuation 
Adam Liebowitz and Kate Lerner applied for a Certificate of Appropriateness to install heat pump and 
exterior conduits after the fact. 
 
Mr. Murray recused from discussion. 
 
Mike Meuse of 128 Home Services/Plumbing and Heating was also present.  A site visit had occurred in 
the interim to discuss interior installing of line sets.  Mr. Liebowitz was in favor of painting the existing 
line sets rather than moving the line sets inside, opining that they were minimally visible from Derby 
Street.   
 
Mr. Meuse delivered talking points from absent colleagues.  Moving existing exterior line sets to the 
building interior would result in exterior patching.  Mr. Meuse also spoke to the difficulty of servicing 
lines located inside walls rather than more easily accessible exterior lines.  Mr. Meuse felt that a portion 
of the line set install resembled that of a downspout.   
 
Chair Tyler-Lewis noted that a building permit was applied for, and thus SHC review was not triggered.  
Mr. Meuse said that the permit not being pulled predated his placement on the team. 
 
Mr. Meche was impressed with the 128 team during the site visit, i.e. their responsiveness to feedback.  
Mr. Meche said that an interior install would not have been that challenging had the SHC been consulted 
in the first place.  Mr. Meche said that exterior line sets were not and never have been desirable to see on 
the outsides of buildings.    
 
Mr. Martinez questioned whether exterior line sets had ever been approved.  Mr. Meche said that owners 
of a Webb Street property had been approved for exterior install yet decided to install inside.  Mr. Meuse 
questioned whether painting to match the exterior would be acceptable.  Mr. Meche questioned the 
Commission’s allowability of granting time to applicants to make building alterations.  Ms. Kelleher said 
that 10 Broad Street was given a long timespan (i.e. more than a year) to resolve outstanding building
Salem Historical Commission Meeting Minutes, November 4, 2026 
Page 3 of 7 
 
modifications.  Mr. Martinez said that a lien could be put on the property, which Ms. Kelleher said was a 
last resort.  Ms. Kelleher clarified that the permitting portal featured “flags” as part of historic properties.  
Mr. Meche proposed providing the applicant a window of time to resolve.  Mr. Leibowitz requested a year 
to complete the revisions.  Mr. Liebowitz said that hiding the line sets would render the CoA no longer 
applicable, in which case Mr. Martinez said a CoNA would be pursued. 
 
Public comment: 
 
Ana Gordan, 12 Crombie, advised the applicant to remove the line sets from the exterior “because they 
look terrible.” 
 
VOTE:  Mr. Meche motioned to grant the applicant 18 months to move the line sets to the interior, in 
which case a Certificate of Non-Applicability would be issued; if work was not completed within 18 
months the applicant would be required to return before the SHC.  Ms. English seconded the motion.  Roll 
Call: English, Meche, Martinez, Peterson, Murray (recused), Tyler-Lewis were in favor and the motion so 
carried. 
 
 
107 Federal Street–continuation 
Susan Hacker applied for a Certificate of Appropriateness for A/C condenser and exterior electrical work 
after the fact.   
 
The applicant requested a continuation to the November 18 meeting. 
 
VOTE:  Mr. Meche motioned to continue the application.  Mr. Murray seconded the motion.  Roll Call: 
Meche, Martinez, Peterson, Murray, Tyler-Lewis were in favor and the motion so carried. 
 
 
396 Essex Street 
Daniel Levitt applied for a Certificate of Appropriateness for door modifications.   
 
Oak double doors especially lower portions were in disrepair, including a piece broken off and dry rot.  
Contractors were not confident that it could be brought up to in-kind work.  Mr. Levitt said the entire 
bottom of each leaf would need to be cut.  Mr. Levitt said that kick plates had been recommended. 
 
Mr. Meche said that kick plates would not stabilize the bottom of the door but would instead trap moisture 
and promote further deterioration of the door.  Mr. Meche recommended a restoration craftsman and 
Woodepox (soft flexible resin).  Door disassembly would be required.  Chair Tyler-Lewis cited a recent 
door restoration to have won an HSI award.  Mr. Murray agreed with Mr. Meche.  Mr. Murray said 
building a new door was significantly more expensive than well-done restoration.  Mr. Levitt reiterated 
that the doors had significant dry rot.  Mr. Meche proposed a site visit.  Mr. Levitt cited other properties 
on Essex Street that featured kick plates on doors. 
 
VOTE:  Mr. Meche motioned to continue the application to the November 18th meeting to conduct a site 
visit.  Ms. English seconded the motion.  Roll Call: English, Meche, Martinez, Peterson, Murray, Tyler-
Lewis were in favor and the motion so carried.
Salem Historical Commission Meeting Minutes, November 4, 2026 
Page 4 of 7 
 
56 Margin Street (including 54 Margin Street, 7 High Street, 20 Endicott Street, 24 Endicott Street)  
Harborlight Homes and Lifebridge applied for a Waiver of the Demolition Delay to demolish two 
buildings older than 50 years; partial demolition of 1 building older than 50 years.   
 
Pat Connolly (Harborlight Homes, project manager) and Stefano Basso (SV Design, project architect) 
were present.  Mr. Connolly delivered a presentation on the project.  Harborlight Homes is a non-profit 
community development corporation based in Beverly, operating throughout the North Shore that builds 
and manages affordable housing for essential workers, elders, families, disabled, etc.  A map of 
Harborlight Homes properties was shown; 11 towns, 760 homes, 1,000 residents, several projects in the 
pipeline, including partnership with Lifebridge.  The corporation integrates supportive services into 
homes to improve their lives and has paid $6M+ in property taxes despite being a non-profit.   
 
The project goals were as follows: create more humane, non congregate shelter with improved 
programming space; significantly improve conditions for the 12 current SRO residents; create 41 new 
permanent supportive housing apartments; and utilize a design on Margin Street featuring 3-4 stories and 
transition into an appearance that matches the neighborhood. 
 
A design history was also recapped that dealt with changes to the scope of the project from 2022-2026. 
March 2023 initial community meetings resulted in keeping the church facade and preserving the church; 
the number of studios was lessened to 46 and then enlarged to 68 (following removal of the thrift store); 
then 53 studios; preserve 20 Endicott facade (in response to feedback from HSI). From late 2025 to 
October 2026 the project had been reviewed by the City Council, 40R approved by EOHLC, PB 
submission, and PB redesign. 
 
Mr. Basso discussed demolition and rebuilding.  Aerial of site plan was shown.  Frontage on Margin 
Street, High Street, and Endicott Street (and Pratt).  Site context was discussed.  Main base of operations 
was shown at Andrew & Carla Oliver Centre.  The decision was made to keep the entire church as a 
central focal point, with additions added to left and right; also maintain the façade of 20 Endicott Street as 
transition from urban core to residential area.  The Christopher Columbus Club building was said to be be 
demolished.  Mr. Basso said that board members, DRB, residents, and neighbors were spoken to 
regarding the importance of Memorial Yard and it would be preserved in the new development.  Views of 
the final design were shown.  Brown brick was shown to match with St. Mary’s.  Mr. Basso said that a 
bad brick match at 20 Endicott facade would be ameliorated. 
 
Mr. Martinez requested clarity on which buildings were getting demolished (Christopher Columbus Club 
and Youth Center) or partially demolished (20 Endicott).  Chair Tyler-Lewis said that some addresses had 
been inventoried and were determined to be potentially eligible for listing in the National Register of 
Historic Places. 
 
Public comment: 
 
Chair Tyler-Lewis read a letter from HSI concerning the property dated 10/19/2026 signed by Richard 
Lindeman.  The letter recognized that the St. Mary’s Church area is a significant group of 100+-year-old 
buildings in Salem that are important to the City’s Italian American history.  The letter implored saving 
St. Mary’s Church and 20 Endicott Street and indicated that Harborlight Homes had committed to 
incorporate facades of both of these historic buildings.  HSI advocated for a design that would reflect 
architectural details to these historic buildings.  HSI preferred robust preservation but opined that this
Salem Historical Commission Meeting Minutes, November 4, 2026 
Page 5 of 7 
 
would not be possible due to significant pressures to develop housing and support services.  HSI urged 
SHC to enforce preservation of facades.   
 
Ms. Kelleher questioned if the church interior was being preserved.  Mr. Basso said that the goal was to 
maintain as much of the church as was possible, though cited interior deterioration.   
 
20 Endicott and 56 Margin were both inventoried, Mr. Martinez said, and lauded preservation of the 
former’s facade.  Ms. Kelleher clarified that all subject buildings had been inventoried, including the 
Christopher Columbus building.  Mr. Martinez commended the public good of the project. 
 
Mr. Connolly clarified that 7 High Street was not part of the project. 
 
Ms. Kelleher said that 54 Margin Street (church) was not to have more than 50% removed and thus 
should not be part of the vote.  
 
No additional public comment. 
 
VOTE:  Ms. English motioned to find 20 Endicott (apartment building, partially preserved), 54 Margin 
(church), 56 Margin (academic building to be demolished), and 24 Endicott (Christopher Columbus 
building) historically significant.  Mr. Martinez seconded the motion.  Roll Call: English, Meche, 
Martinez, Peterson, Murray, Tyler-Lewis were in favor and the motion so carried. 
 
Mr. Meche said that Seeds of Hope at 7 Crombie had been purchased 20 years prior and was reminiscent 
of the academic building at 56 Margin.  Mr. Meche felt that 24 Endicott could be demolished.  Overall, 
Mr. Meche was supportive of the application.  Mr. Peterson agreed with Mr. Meche.  Ms. Kelleher said 
that review of preferable preservation should consider whether the building was a great example of its 
type, retained its historical integrity, and other criteria.   
 
VOTE:  Mr. Martinez motioned to find the buildings in question not preferably preserved, excepting the 
stated conditions on facade preservation.  Mr. Meche seconded the motion.  Roll Call: English (no), 
Meche, Martinez, Peterson, Murray, Tyler-Lewis were in favor and the motion so carried. 
 
Ms. Kelleher said that MHC had requested SHC comments on the project. 
 
 
21 Warren Street 
Carrie and Lee Dichter applied for a Certificate of Hardship for chimney removal.  
 
The applicants requested a continuation to the November 18 meeting. 
 
VOTE:  Mr. Peterson motioned to continue the application to the November 18th meeting.  Mr. Murray 
seconded the motion.  Roll Call: Meche, Martinez, Peterson, Murray, Tyler-Lewis, English were in favor 
and the motion so carried. 
 
 
11 Summer Street 
Emmerton House LLC applied for a waiver of the Demolition Delay to demolish carriage building older 
than 50 years.
Salem Historical Commission Meeting Minutes, November 4, 2026 
Page 6 of 7 
 
 
The applicants requested to withdraw the application. 
 
VOTE:  Mr. Meche motioned to accept the withdrawal.  Mr. Martinez seconded the motion.  Roll Call: 
All were in favor and the motion so carried. 
 
 
7 Carpenter Street 
Patricia McCosco applied for a Certificate of Appropriateness to replace the condenser with a heat pump 
(after the fact).   
 
Ms. Kelleher proposed a continuation in the applicant’s absence. 
 
VOTE:  Ms. English  motioned to continue the application to the November 18th meeting.  Mr. Peterson 
seconded the motion.  Roll Call: English, Meche, Martinez, Peterson, Murray, Tyler-Lewis were in favor 
and the motion so carried. 
 
 
Request for CLG (Certified Local Government) Opinion 
National Register Nomination Church of the Immaculate Conception Complex.   
 
The consultant (historic tax credit project for school building–St. Mary’s School) was not present but had 
delivered an extensive historical significance statement.  Eligible due to association with events, patterns 
of history, and architectural style.  Enoch Fuller and Jonathan Gray were architects for the buildings.  Ms. 
English said that the complex had received an HSI award in the past.  Mr. Meche identified the build date 
of the church as 1857; school 1941; rectory on Union Street 1858/1973.   
 
VOTE:  Ms. English motioned to provide a CLG opinion supporting the complex eligibility.  Mr. 
Martinez seconded the motion.  Roll Call: English, Martinez, Meche, Peterson, Murray, Tyler-Lewis were 
in favor and the motion so carried. 
 
 
Request for comment - FY27 Community Preservation Act Plan   
 
Ms. Kelleher noted previous comments to continue prioritization of CPA funds to stabilize and preserve 
the City’s vacant and underutilized historic buildings and resources; as well as utilizing CPA funds to 
establish a local preservation grant program for historic district property owners similar to programs in 
Cambridge and Springfield.  Ms. English asked about the City’s digitization project for the historic 
building documents. Ms. Kelleher said that the digitization project was multi-phased; first of which was 
cataloguing every building plan and permit in the collection.  The City was seeking funding to commence 
digitization of records.  Mr. Meche noted a recent demo delay of a GI Bill Memorial Drive Cape Cod and 
articulated the need to consolidate SHC’s position on such projects.  Chair Tyler-Lewis approached 
working with HSI to raise community consciousness or public education of such architecture, such as 
adding such styles to their website’s architectural glossary.   
 
Ms. Kelleher stated that she would draft a comment letter for the Commission to consider.
Salem Historical Commission Meeting Minutes, November 4, 2026 
Page 7 of 7 
 
Other Business 
 
St. Nicholas Church 
 
Mr. Martinez learned that the property owner(s) would not demolish the three-story building but rather 
redevelop and make it house people again. 
 
Minutes 
 
VOTE:  Ms. English motioned to approve the October 7 minutes.  Mr. Meche seconded the motion.  Roll 
Call: English, Meche, Martinez, Peterson, Murray, Tyler-Lewis were in favor and the motion so carried. 
 
Letter to Mass SAVE 
Ms. Kelleher was drafting a letter expressing SHC concern about the number of installations sponsored by 
Mass SAVE in the City without permits, cc’ing the Mayor, Building Commissioner, and Director of 
Sustainability and Resiliency. 
 
Ms. Kelleher reported that the Fort Lee Preservation Plan was recently completed.  Recommendations 
included looking to secure physical fort area to keep people from accessing earthworks (i.e. fencing), 
limiting clearing to preserve the tree coverage to allow views into the fort, and increased interpretive 
signage.   
 
Ms. Kelleher also shared the goal of securing architect for the Winter Island Hangar and beginning 
construction on structural repairs in early spring 2027.   
 
Scaffolding came down on Dickson Chapel in Greenlawn Cemetery.  Ribbon cutting to be held on 
November 14, 2026. 
 
 
 
Adjournment 
 
VOTE:  Ms. English motioned to adjourn.  Mr. Meche seconded the motion.  Roll Call: English, 
Peterson, Meche, Martinez, Gonzalez, Tyler-Lewis were in favor and the motion so carried. 
 
The meeting adjourned at 8:33PM. 
 
 
 
Respectfully submitted, 
Dan Graham, Historical Commission Clerk
